look_here_first: LOOK HERE FIRST · An UNARMED herb with ALTERNATE simple green ovate leaves and little WHITE five-lobed flowers. Its yellow anthers are distinctly longer than those of American black nightshade (typically 1.8–2.5 mm versus ca. 0.8–1.5 mm). CONFIRM with mature fruit: S. nigrescens usually has DULL green/dark purplish berries, calyx lobes APPRESSED or spreading against the berry base, and fruit pedicels that spread or droop. S. americanum usually has shiny black berries with tiny calyx lobes STRONGLY REFLEXED backward. Do not assign species confidently from white flowers or immature fruit alone.

project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Current learner is encounter-based; do not claim verified Hays County nativity or calculate native scores.

morphology_keys.family_pattern: Solanaceae/Solanum: mostly alternate foliage, fused five-lobed corolla, five poricidal anthers, and multi-seeded berry; Morelloid black nightshades are unarmed.
best_field_traits: Green unarmed branching herb/short-lived perennial; simple alternate ovate leaves, margins entire to shallowly toothed
White 5-lobed rotate/star corolla with projecting yellow relatively elongated anthers
Anthers generally 1.8–2.5 mm, elliptic, not almost globose short anthers as in S. americanum
Fruit ultimately commonly dark purplish or green/dull rather than glossy black; fruit clusters often have spreading/deflexed stalks
Calyx lobes below ripe berry APPRESSED to SPREADING, not strongly reflexed backwards
More than five hard sclerotic granules (stone cells) often in berry; specialist character, not a tasting or field-food lesson
morphology_keys.habit: Annual or short-lived perennial herb, branching, green, unarmed; stems may be sparsely hairy. Habit alone overlaps the Solanum morelloid group.
morphology_keys.leaves: ALTERNATE simple ovate or elliptic green leaves, entire to wavy/toothed edges, pointed tips, petioles evident. Do not call the species from leaves alone.
morphology_keys.flowers: Small white five-part star flowers, clustered; five equal elongated yellow anthers approximately 1.8–2.5 mm long; pale style projects centrally. Flower macros can show relative size, but no quantitative length is proved without a scale.
morphology_keys.fruit: Immature green berries; mature dark purple to black, often dull/glaucous rather than shiny. Fruiting pedicels spreading or deflexed (tend to depart with fallen berries). The short green calyx lobes remain appressed or spreading under the mature fruit, NOT sharply curled away as typical in S. americanum.
morphology_keys.habitat: Fields, open woodland edges, disturbed and moist areas, forest margins. Flora of North America reports Texas but Hays-local nativity verification deferred.
morphology_keys.management: Do not recommend consuming any part based on image ID. Black-nightshade species overlap and their chemistry varies. Field crew: photograph reproductive structures, avoid bare-handed tasting, and make management decisions after firm ID.

field_terms.Anther: Yellow pollen-producing organ; compare LENGTH and shape against S. americanum, ideally with a millimeter scale.
field_terms.Calyx: Green SEPALS under flower or berry; appressed = pressed close to berry, reflexed = bent sharply backward.
field_terms.Pedicel: Little individual flower/berry stalk; inspect whether it spreads/droops and stays with fruit when it drops.
field_terms.Sclerotic granules: Small hard stone cells inside a berry, NOT the seeds; laboratory-level character, not photographed/verified in this card.
field_terms.Morelloid group: Close unarmed black-nightshade species; white stars and black berries alone are not exact IDs.

crew_field_sequence: 1 · Whole plant: unarmed green herb with simple alternate leaves. If prickly, compare the other Solanum cards.
2 · Open flower: find 5 white lobes and the yellow ANTHERS; take a macro with a millimeter scale.
3 · Flower comparison: S. nigrescens anthers usually about 1.8–2.5 mm versus S. americanum short plump ~0.8–1.5 mm.
4 · Mature berry: photograph side view showing fruit luster and green CALYX LOBES; nigrescens calyx typically appressed/spreading.
5 · Fruiting cluster: photograph pedicel direction and stalk attachment. Drooping fruit with calyx close to berry supports nigrescens over americanum.
6 · If only white flower or immature green fruit is visible: record Solanum morelloid complex and return with macro/ripe fruit evidence.
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Hard pair: American black nightshade. Longer anthers + appressed/spreading calyx + duller fruit + spreading/deflexed pedicels favor nigrescens.

field_matrix.flower: White star, ellipsoid LONGER anthers typically 1.8–2.5 mm
field_matrix.berries: Usually matte/dull dark purplish or green mature berry
field_matrix.calyx: Short lobes APPRESSED to SPREADING at berry base
field_matrix.pedicels: Spreading or bent downward; often drop with berry
field_matrix.quick_rule: Longer anthers + calyx touching berry + dull fruit together.

field_matrix.flower: Tiny white star; plump SHORT anthers ~0.8–1.5 mm
field_matrix.calyx: Tiny lobes STRONGLY REFLEXED away from mature berry
field_matrix.pedicels: Spreading/erect, often remain on shoot after fruit drops
field_matrix.quick_rule: Very short anthers + glossy berry + backwards calyx.

field_matrix.flower: Short yellow anthers overlap S. americanum, filaments usually relatively longer
field_matrix.berries: Matte dark fruit, typically more stone cells
field_matrix.quick_rule: Short anthers + dull fruit and calyx appressed; harder with only photos.

field_matrix.taxon: Solanum interius · CENTRAL PLAINS BLACK NIGHTSHADE
field_matrix.berries: Often larger ripe fruit; internal granules differ
field_matrix.calyx: Frequently unequal calyx lobes with rounded tips
field_matrix.quick_rule: Regional look-alike; larger berries, unequal rounded-tipped calyx lobes.

field_matrix.flower: Medium yellow anthers, inflorescence frequently more elongated
field_matrix.berries: Often matte black; lacks stone cells
field_matrix.quick_rule: Introduced comparison; do not identify by black ripe berries alone.

field_matrix.flower: Large bright yellow flower with ONE long curved anther
field_matrix.quick_rule: Yellow corolla plus spiny fruit enclosure.

not_reliable_alone: WHITE flowers alone: shared across morelloids.
One green immature fruit: not diagnostic.
Black berry alone: both species and more have dark berries.
Size of anther without measurement: use scale and compare same angle.
Fruit from photographs taken in different lighting can look glossy or dull differently.

items.caption: EXACT-SPECIES research photograph of THREE RIPE dark-purple/black S. nigrescens berries. Five green calyx lobes remain spread against the fruit BASE, not strongly reflexed backwards like typical American black nightshade. The 5 mm bar belongs to the original scientific figure; no invented enlargement scale. Photo source: Ramírez-Olvera & Sandoval-Villa (2023), Plants 12(8):1645. Cropped/converted as indicated, CC BY 4.0.
items.why_it_matters: Use fruiting calyx orientation and surface texture with measured flower anthers to separate divine from American black nightshade. A calyx contact trait is better than black color alone.
